transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the Overview expanded, with its source cards
d: THE NAME, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The term eclipse archive can refer to several distinct topics depending on the context:' Five bullets: 'Poetry & Digital Archives: The Eclipse Archive is a digital poetry publisher and archive founded by Craig Dworkin and edited by Danny Snelson, featuring out-of-print and avant-garde writing (such as Gnome Baker magazine)'; the Eclipse Foundation's project archives; 'Eclipse Archives', a streetwear brand of anime drops; NASA's Historical Eclipse Image Archive; Eclipse IDE archive tools. Eight cards: eclipsearchive.org, the brand's shop, NASA, the Eclipse Foundation (two), the Eclipse Marketplace (two), TikTok.
reading: The innocent reading first. Given a two-word name shared by a software foundation, a clothing brand, a solar image archive and IDE plugins, the Overview lists the senses it finds and asks which one the user means.
findings: THE ARCHIVE ONE SENSE OF FIVE. The poetry archive leads the list ('Poetry & Digital Archives') and holds one bullet and one card of eight; the rest of the field at the name is the Eclipse Foundation's 'historical builds, discontinued software releases, and source files', the brand's 'anime-themed drops such as Jujutsu Kaisen (JJK) collections', NASA's photographs 'dating back to 1869' and two Marketplace plugins.

THE EDITORS AT THEIR GRAIN. 'founded by Craig Dworkin and edited by Danny Snelson' stands as the home page has it: 'Founding Editor: Craig Dworkin Editor: Danny Snelson'. 'such as Gnome Baker magazine' is the home page's one notice: 'NEW TO THE ARCHIVE: The first issue of the fugitive Gnome Baker magazine, from October, 1976.'

PUBLISHER AND ARCHIVE, WITHOUT ITS PURPOSE. 'a digital poetry publisher and archive' agrees with Wikipedia's account, which the census holds: 'Eclipse later expanded to publish selected new works and born-digital publications in the spirit of those earlier presses.' The same sentence's first half is absent from the composition: 'Dworkin started the archive in 2002 to provide readers and scholars with access to avant-garde works that were no longer available in print from their original publishers'. So are the facsimile form ('high-resolution scans of every page of its included texts, most from Dworkin's personal collection') and the name's homage to 'Douglas Messerli ’s Sun & Moon press'.

THE AUTHOR INDEX NOT CARRIED. The census reads Eclipse for its index, where a co-written title stands under every collaborator ('LEGEND [with Charles Bernstein, Ray DiPalma, Steve McCaffery, and Ron Silliman]' under Bruce Andrews, 'Ray DiPalma LEGEND [with Bruce Andrews, Charles Bernstein, Steve McCaffery, and Ron Silliman]' under DiPalma) and a translation under its translator ('Rosmarie Waldrop (trans.) The Dilemma of Being High and Dry') as well as its author. The card's snippet opens on the site's navigation, 'Eclipse ECLIPSE Authors Titles', and the composition gives no account of it.
analysis: A disambiguation in which the poetry archive leads, its editors and newest item correct. Its purpose, its 2002 start and the author index that holds each collaborator and translator under a name of their own are not in the composition.
per_note: Both editors named; no institution; the archive's home page carded once among seven other Eclipse sources.
